In mathematics, '''Gelfand–Fuks cohomology''', introduced by [[Israel Gelfand]] and [[Dmitry Fuchs]] in {{harv|Gel'fand|Fuks|1969–70}}, is a [[cohomology]] theory for [[Lie algebras]] of smooth [[vector field]]s.  It differs from the [[Lie algebra cohomology]] of Chevalley-Eilenberg in that its cochains are taken to be continuous <math>\mathbb{R}-</math>multilinear alternating forms on the Lie algebra of smooth vector fields where the latter is given the <math>C^{\infty}</math> topology.
